name: PINNACLE
question: Does paclitaxel-coated balloon dilation of the prostatic urethra improve lower urinary tract symptoms from BPH more than a sham procedure?

design.blinding: double-blind (participants and evaluating personnel) through 12 months

arms.label: sham cystoscopic procedure with an uninflated predilation catheter

design.population: 148 men aged 50 to 80 years with symptomatic BPH, IPSS of 13 or more, Qmax 5 to 12 mL/s, prostate volume 20 to 80 g and prostatic urethral length 32 to 55 mm.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized device trial
design.locator: J Urol full text, Materials and Methods and Results (Demographics and Procedure)

verdictNote: Primary endpoint missed with the 25% sham margin; secondary endpoints were not formally tested.
takeaway: In men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms, Optilume BPH paclitaxel-coated balloon dilation improved IPSS by 11.5 points at 12 months versus 8.0 points with a sham procedure at 3 months, but missed its primary endpoint, which added a 25% margin to the sham effect.

reports.label: 12-month randomized comparison
reports.citation: Kaplan SA, Moss J, Freedman S, et al. "The PINNACLE Study: A Double-blind, Randomized, Sham-controlled Study Evaluating the Optilume BPH Catheter System for the Treatment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Secondary to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *J Urol.* 2023;210(3):500-509. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000003568
reports.followUp: 12 months (Optilume BPH arm) versus 3 months (sham arm, the primary comparison time point)
reports.followUpLocator: J Urol full text, Statistical Methods and Efficacy

results.measure: IPSS improvement from baseline, Optilume BPH at 12 months versus sham at 3 months, with a prespecified 25% super-superiority margin on the sham effect; difference = Optilume BPH minus sham with margin
results.note: The sham effect with the 25% margin was 10.0 points. The journal reports P = .18 for the margin-adjusted comparison; the difference, interval and exact P come from the FDA summary of safety and effectiveness, Table 12.
results.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Efficacy); FDA SSED P220029 p 27 of 46, Table 12

results.measure: IPSS improvement without the margin, Optilume BPH at 12 months minus sham at 3 months
results.note: Intention-to-treat with multiple imputation; alternative therapy counted as no improvement. Nominal P value.

results.measure: Mean percent IPSS improvement from baseline to 12 months in the Optilume BPH arm against a prespecified performance goal of 30%
results.note: The journal reports the goal as met (nominal P); the FDA summary states that secondary hypotheses were not formally tested because the primary endpoint was not met.
results.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Efficacy); FDA SSED P220029 p 28 of 46

results.measure: Participants with at least 30% IPSS improvement, Optilume BPH at 12 months versus sham at 3 months
results.note: The journal text prints the Optilume BPH numerator and denominator as 66/96 with 76.6%; 66/96 is the 3-month responder count (68.8%) in the FDA summary, whose Table 17 gives 72/94 at 12 months. Hypothesis not formally tested.
results.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Efficacy); FDA SSED P220029 pp 28-29 of 46, Tables 16-17

results.measure: Qmax change from baseline, Optilume BPH at 12 months versus sham at 3 months; difference = Optilume BPH minus sham
results.note: Voids under 150 mL excluded. The FDA summary lists the estimate as sham minus Optilume BPH, -4.2 (95% CI -7.6 to -0.8); the sign is reversed here. Hypothesis not formally tested.
results.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Efficacy); FDA SSED P220029 p 29 of 46, Table 18

results.measure: Paired IPSS change from baseline at 12 months, Optilume BPH arm
results.note: Within-arm paired analysis of participants with a 12-month visit; no concurrent sham value at 12 months.

results.measure: Paired IPSS quality-of-life change from baseline at 12 months, Optilume BPH arm
Paired Qmax change from baseline at 12 months, Optilume BPH arm
Paired postvoid residual change from baseline at 12 months, Optilume BPH arm
Sham-arm IPSS improvement from baseline at 12 months
results.note: Compared with 8.0 points (33.3%) at 3 months in the same arm.

results.measure: IIEF erectile function domain change from baseline at 12 months
results.note: The authors report no significant differences between arms.

results.measure: MSHQ-EjD function score change from baseline at 12 months
results.note: The authors report no significant differences between arms; the MSHQ-EjD bother score changed -0.6 ± 1.7 (n=87) and -0.5 ± 2.1 (n=26).

harms.label: Serious adverse events judged related to the device
harms.note: Four postprocedural hematuria events needing cystoscopic management or extended observation, which resolved without sequelae, and one urethral false passage needing extended catheterization. The FDA summary also lists one grade 3 bladder perforation adjudicated as procedure-related, giving 6/98 (6.1%) treatment-related serious events. No participant met the prespecified composite of major device-related complications.
harms.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Safety and Tolerability); FDA SSED P220029 pp 20-22 of 46, Tables 9-11

harms.label: Hematuria (any, regardless of relatedness)
harms.note: Usually mild to moderate and resolved within 1 month in the journal. In the FDA as-treated analysis, treatment-related hematuria occurred in 39/98 (39.8%) as 41 events, 37/41 mild or moderate, with median 34 days to resolution. Serious hematuria became less frequent after mild-to-moderate Foley traction and bladder flushing were adopted.
harms.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Safety) and Discussion; FDA SSED P220029 pp 22-24 of 46

harms.label: Urinary tract infection (any, regardless of relatedness)
harms.note: Treatment-related urinary tract infection in the FDA summary: 11/98 (11.2%) with Optilume BPH versus 2/48 (4.2%) with sham.
harms.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Safety); FDA SSED P220029 p 23 of 46, Table 12

harms.label: Ejaculatory dysfunction (adverse event)
harms.note: P > .9. No treatment-related de novo erectile dysfunction was reported.
harms.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Safety and Tolerability)

harms.label: Urethral stricture (treatment-related)
harms.locator: FDA SSED P220029 p 25 of 46, Table 12

harms.label: Urinary retention (treatment-related)
harms.locator: FDA SSED P220029 p 25 of 46, Table 12

harms.label: Mean maximum plasma paclitaxel concentration (pharmacokinetic subset)
harms.note: Median 1 hour after treatment; average plasma concentration was below the limit of quantitation by Foley removal.
harms.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Safety and Tolerability)

delivery.label: Device and technique
delivery.value: Rigid 20F cystoscopy; uncoated predilation balloon inflated for about 1 minute to initiate an anterior commissurotomy; 90F drug-coated balloon, 30 to 45 mm long by transrectal-ultrasound prostatic urethral length, inflated for at least 5 minutes; Foley catheter for 2 days.
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Materials and Methods (Optilume BPH Treatment Procedure)

delivery.label: Anesthesia
delivery.note: Deep sedation or general anesthesia (P = .9); moderate sedation and local prostate block were used at a similar rate in each arm.
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Demographics and Procedure)

delivery.label: Procedure time (scope in to scope out)
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Demographics and Procedure)

delivery.label: Duration of catheterization
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Demographics and Procedure)

delivery.label: Sham procedure
delivery.value: Rigid cystoscopy with a sheathed 21F predilation catheter that was not inflated, held for about 5 minutes; Foley catheter for 2 days; scripted staff dialogue, a drape blocking the participant's view, and identical analgesia and catheterization protocols.
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Materials and Methods (Sham Treatment Procedure)

delivery.label: Blinding at Foley removal
delivery.value: All sham participants believed they had received Optilume BPH or were unsure; 62.5% at 3 months.
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Results (Demographics and Procedure)

delivery.label: Crossover
delivery.value: Sham participants could break the blind and cross to Optilume BPH after the 3-month visit; 20 of the 48 did so before their 12-month visit.
delivery.locator: J Urol full text, Materials and Methods (Assessments and Follow-up); count from FDA SSED P220029 p 16 of 46

reports.label: 2-year follow-up

reports.followUp: 2 years, Optilume BPH arm only (2-year data for 77 of 100; IPSS in 74)
reports.followUpLocator: Prostate Cancer Prostatic Dis full text (PMC11319191), Methods and Results

results.measure: At least 30% IPSS improvement without medical or surgical retreatment at 2 years; treatment failures counted in the denominator
results.note: Among participants with observed 2-year IPSS, 57/74 (77%) had at least 30% improvement.

results.measure: Paired IPSS change from baseline at 2 years
results.note: The text reports a 50.8% improvement and unpaired means of 23.4 ± 5.5 (n=100) to 11.0 ± 7.0 (n=74).

results.measure: Paired Qmax change from baseline at 2 years
results.note: Voids under 150 mL excluded. The text reports a 116.8% improvement.

results.note: Surgical reinterventions included prostatic artery embolization, TURP and laser ablation.

harms.note: 41 events in 39 participants, 37/41 mild or moderate, median 34 days to resolution, no transfusions; frequency fell after the traction and bladder-flushing protocol was adopted.
